extracted.intended_audience: issuers (SEC registrants), corporate counsel, accountants, and SEC filing compliance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Item-by-item regulatory instructions governing the non‑financial content of Securities Act and Exchange Act registration statements, reports, prospectuses, and related filings (Regulation S‑K). Covers business, securities, financial, management, prospectus, exhibits, industry-specific, roll‑up, M‑A, asset‑backed, oil & gas/mining/bank disclosures and SPAC/de‑SPAC requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Regulation S-K (Item 10 General)
rubrics_metrics.description: This part states the requirements applicable to the content of the non‑financial statement portions of: (1) registration statements under the Securities Act to the extent provided in the forms; and (2) registration statements under section 12, annual or other reports under sections 13 and 15(d), going‑private transaction statements, tender offer statements, annual reports to security holders and proxy and information statements and any other documents required to be filed under the Exchange Act, to the extent provided in the forms and rules under that Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope note: read in conjunction with related General Rules and Regulations under the Securities Act and Exchange Act, Interpretative Releases, and forms. Electronic filers must also consult Regulation S‑T (Part 232).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission policy on projections (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission encourages use of management's projections of future economic performance that have a reasonable basis and are presented in an appropriate format; guidelines set forth are factors to consider in formulating and disclosing such projections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements on (1) basis for projections (management must have a reasonable basis; outside review may support basis and, if included, must disclose reviewer's qualifications, extent, relationship and consent when required) and (2) format for projections: consider financial items to be projected, period covered, manner of presentation; projections need not be limited to revenues, net income and EPS but be careful to avoid selective projection of only favorable items; disclose most probable amount or most reasonable range based on assumptions; ranges should not be so wide as to be meaningless; multiple projections based on varying assumptions may be permitted; distinguish projections not based on historical results from those that are; present historical results with equal or greater prominence when projections rely on them; non‑GAAP projected measures must include definition, GAAP comparable, and explanation of why non‑GAAP selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission policy on security ratings (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants may voluntarily disclose ratings assigned by rating organizations to classes of debt securities, convertible debt securities and preferred stock; Commission sets forth matters to consider in disclosing security ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Securities Act filings: consider including any other materially different rating available on initial filing date; include name of each rating organization, each rating organization's definition of category, relative rank in that organization's system, and a statement that a rating is not a recommendation and may be revised or withdrawn; include written consent of any non‑NRSRO rating organization; consider including rating changes in final prospectus or amending registration statement if material. For Exchange Act filings: consider similar information; disclose material rating changes by Form 8‑K or other appropriate report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of non‑GAAP financial measures in Commission filings (Item 10(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever one or more non‑GAAP financial measures are included in a filing, the registrant must include specified reconciliations and disclosures and must not engage in certain practices with respect to non‑GAAP measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required when non‑GAAP measures are used: (A) present, with equal or greater prominence, the most directly comparable GAAP measure; (B) provide a reconciliation (quantitative for historical measures; quantitative to extent available for forward‑looking); (C) statement of reasons management believes non‑GAAP provides useful information; (D) disclose additional management uses if material. Prohibitions include: excluding charges or liabilities requiring (or that would have required) cash settlement from non‑GAAP liquidity measures except EBIT/EBITDA; adjusting measures to eliminate/smooth items identified as non‑recurring when nature of charge/gain is reasonably likely to recur within two years or there was a similar item within prior two years; presenting non‑GAAP measures on the face of GAAP financial statements or pro forma financial information required by Article 11 of Regulation S‑X; using titles/descriptions for non‑GAAP measures that are the same as or confusingly similar to GAAP measures. Exceptions and definitions are provided (foreign private issuers, investment companies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scaled disclosure for smaller reporting companies (Item 10(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of Regulation S‑K apply to smaller reporting companies, which may comply with either scaled requirements for smaller reporting companies or the full requirements for other companies, except where specified otherwise. The regulation provides an index of items with scaled disclosure available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: issuer that is not an investment company, asset‑backed issuer, or certain subsidiaries and that had either public float < $250M or annual revenues < $100M and either no public float or public float < $700M. Determination rules: measurement dates (last business day of most recently completed second fiscal quarter for public float; audited annual revenues for most recently completed fiscal year) and required disclosure of determination in Form 10‑Q cover page and subsequent filings; special rules for initial registration statements and re‑determination options. Lists specific items for which scaled disclosure is available (Item 101, 201, 302, 305, 402, 404, 407, 503, 504, 601).

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1600) Subpart header: Special Purpose Acquisition Companies (SPACs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart 229.1600—Special Purpose Acquisition Companies. Items 1601–1610 set forth SPAC and de‑SPAC disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1602) Registered offerings by special purpose acquisition companies
rubrics_metrics.description: (Item 1602) Registered offerings by special purpose acquisition companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross‑referenced elsewhere (e.g., offering price disclosure, prospectus requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1603) SPAC sponsor; conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the amount of securities issued or to be issued by the SPAC to the SPAC sponsor, its affiliates, and promoters and the price paid or to be paid for such securities in connection with the de‑SPAC transaction or any related financing transaction; disclose whether this compensation and securities issuance may result in a material dilution of the equity interests of non‑redeeming shareholders; provide cross‑references to related prospectus disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also require statement of any actual or potential material conflicts of interest that may arise (including compensation arrangements) between SPAC sponsors/affiliates/officers/directors/promoters/target company officers and unaffiliated SPAC security holders; highlight cross‑references to related disclosures prominently.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1604) Prospects summary and dilution in de‑SPAC transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospectus summary must include in plain English the background and material terms of the de‑SPAC transaction, board determinations and material factors considered, material conflicts of interest, tabular presentation of sponsor compensation and securities issuance and how that may dilute non‑redeeming shareholders, material financing terms and anticipated use of proceeds, and rights of security holders to redeem; disclose dilution in tabular format with intervals representing selected potential redemption levels across a reasonably likely range and provide model description, methods, assumptions, estimates and parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabular dilution must show offering price, net tangible book value per share as adjusted for redemption levels (excluding the de‑SPAC itself), nature/amounts of each source of dilution and number of shares used; outside the table describe each material potential source of future dilution not included in table; for each redemption level state the company valuation at/above which non‑redeeming shareholders' interest per share is at least the IPO price; describe model/methods/assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1605) Background of and reasons for the de‑SPAC transaction; terms of the de‑SPAC transaction; effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide summary of background (contacts, negotiations, transactions), state material terms (brief description of transaction and related financing, payments from sponsor to investors, reasons for structure/timing), explain material differences in rights of SPAC vs combined company security holders, brief accounting treatment statement, and Federal income tax consequences to SPAC, target and security holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe effects of transaction and related financing on SPAC and affiliates, sponsor and affiliates, target company and affiliates, and unaffiliated security holders, discussing benefits and detriments quantified to extent practicable; disclose material interests held by sponsors/officers/directors/target officers; state whether security holders have redemption or appraisal rights and summarize those rights or other remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1606) Board determination about the de‑SPAC transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If law requires the board (or similar governing body) to determine whether the de‑SPAC transaction is advisable and in holders' best interests, disclose that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss material factors considered by the board (including valuation, financial projections relied upon, financing terms, any report/opinion/appraisal, and dilution); state whether approval of at least a majority of unaffiliated security holders is required; state whether a majority of independent directors retained an unaffiliated representative for unaffiliated holders; disclose whether de‑SPAC was approved by a majority of non‑employee directors and identify any voting against or abstentions and reasons if known after reasonable inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1607) Reports, opinions, appraisals, and negotiations (SPACs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If SPAC or sponsor received any report, opinion (other than counsel), or appraisal from an outside party or unaffiliated representative materially relating to board determinations, approval, consideration/fairness of consideration to be offered to target security holders, or fairness to SPAC/security holders/sponsor, disclose specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each report/opinion/appraisal/negotiation: identify outside party/unauthorized representative; describe qualifications; describe method of selection; disclose material relationships and compensation between the preparer and SPAC/sponsor/affiliates; state whether outside party recommended valuation or amount of consideration or whether SPAC determined valuations; furnish summary of procedures, findings, recommendations, bases/methods for findings, instructions received and any scope limitations. Instruction: provide firm‑level information (firm providing report) rather than individual preparers. All such reports/opinions/appraisals must be filed as exhibits to the registration statement or schedule if exhibit filing required.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1608) Tender offer filing obligations (SPACs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the SPAC files a Schedule TO for any redemption of securities offered to security holders, such Schedule TO must provide the information required by General Instruction L.2. to Form S‑4, General Instruction I.2. to Form F‑4, and Item 14(f)(2) of Schedule 14A, as applicable, in addition to information otherwise required by Schedule TO, and such redemptions must comply with applicable Rule 13e‑4 and Regulation 14E provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1609) Projections in de‑SPAC transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to any projections disclosed in the filing (or exhibits), disclose the purpose for which projections were prepared and the party that prepared them; disclose all material bases and assumptions and any material factors that may affect such assumptions, including discussion of growth/reduction/discount rates and reasons for selecting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If projections relate to the SPAC, state whether projections reflect the view of SPAC management/board as of the most recent practicable date; if projections relate to the target, disclose whether the target affirmed that projections reflect its management/board view; if projections no longer reflect such views, state the purpose for disclosing and reasons for continued reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Item 1610) Structured data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the disclosure required by this subpart in an Interactive Data File in accordance with §§ 232.405 (Rule 405 of Regulation S‑T) and 232.301 (the EDGAR Filer Manual).
